aboutAuthors: Google Brain, Google Research and University of Toronto. Introduced the Transformer, the architecture underlying nearly all current large language models.
authors: Vaswani, Shazeer, Parmar, Uszkoreit, Jones, Gomez, Kaiser, Polosukhin
hook: A sequence transduction model built only from attention and feed-forward layers: no recurrence, no convolutions.

insights.body: In an RNN, h_t depends on h_(t-1), so a layer needs O(n) sequential operations and cannot be parallelised across positions during training. The path between two distant tokens is O(n), which makes long-range dependencies hard to learn. Convolutional seq2seq models (ConvS2S, ByteNet) parallelise, but the path length grows as O(n/k) or O(log_k n). Self-attention connects any two positions in O(1) sequential operations, at O(n²·d) cost per layer, which is cheaper than recurrent O(n·d²) whenever n < d.
insights.headline: Recurrence is the bottleneck

insights.body: Each token is projected to a query, key and value. The output is a weighted sum of values, with weights from the softmax over query-key similarities. The 1/√d_k scaling matters: if q and k have unit-variance components, q·k has variance d_k, so for large d_k the softmax saturates and gradients vanish. Dot-product attention was preferred over additive attention because it is a single matrix multiplication and runs fast on GPUs.
insights.headline: Scaled dot-product attention

insights.body: Instead of one attention with d_model-dimensional keys, the model learns h=8 sets of projections W_i^Q, W_i^K, W_i^V into d_k=d_v=64 dimensions, runs attention in each in parallel, concatenates the results and applies W^O. Total cost matches single-head full-dimension attention, but each head can attend to a different representation subspace. It is used three ways: encoder self-attention, decoder self-attention with a causal mask (setting illegal softmax inputs to −∞ to preserve autoregression), and encoder-decoder cross-attention where queries come from the decoder and keys and values from the encoder.
insights.headline: Multi-head attention

insights.body: Each of the N=6 encoder layers has a self-attention sublayer and a position-wise feed-forward network applied independently to every position (d_model=512, d_ff=2048). Each sublayer is wrapped in a residual connection followed by layer normalisation. The decoder adds a cross-attention sublayer between the two. The residual stream keeps every sublayer output in d_model=512 dimensions, which makes the stacking uniform.
insights.headline: Block structure: residuals, LayerNorm, FFN

insights.body: Attention is permutation-invariant, so order must be injected. The paper adds fixed sinusoids of geometrically spaced wavelengths (from 2π to 10000·2π) to the token embeddings. The authors hypothesised this lets the model attend by relative offset, since PE(pos+k) is a linear function of PE(pos). Learned positional embeddings performed nearly identically, but sinusoids might extrapolate to longer sequences than seen in training.
insights.headline: Positional encoding

insights.body: Adam with β1=0.9, β2=0.98, ε=1e-9 and a schedule with linear warm-up for 4000 steps followed by inverse-square-root decay. Regularisation: residual dropout 0.1 and label smoothing 0.1 (which hurts perplexity but improves BLEU). Data: WMT14 EN-DE with about 4.5M sentence pairs and a shared 37k BPE vocabulary, and EN-FR with 36M pairs and a 32k word-piece vocabulary. Decoding uses beam search (beam 4, length penalty 0.6), and the final models average checkpoints.
insights.headline: Training recipe

lesson: The key design question is the length of the path between any two inputs, and how much of the computation can run in parallel. Attention makes the first O(1) at the price of quadratic cost in sequence length.
limitations: Self-attention costs O(n²) time and memory in sequence length, which limits context size and led to later sparse, linear and IO-aware (FlashAttention) variants. The model has no built-in notion of order or locality beyond positional encodings. Autoregressive decoding is still sequential at inference time. The paper evaluates mainly on machine translation, with only a small constituency-parsing experiment as evidence of generality.

numbers.label: WMT14 English→German
numbers.value: 28.4 BLEU (big), >2 BLEU above prior best incl. ensembles

numbers.label: WMT14 English→French
numbers.value: ≈41 BLEU single model, new state of the art

numbers.label: Training cost
numbers.value: Base: 12 h on 8 P100 GPUs. Big: 3.5 days

numbers.label: Complexity per layer
numbers.value: O(n²·d) compute, O(1) sequential ops, O(1) path length

summary: The Transformer replaces recurrence with stacked multi-head self-attention and position-wise feed-forward layers, joined by residual connections and LayerNorm, with positional encodings for order. It reduces sequential operations per layer to O(1), parallelises training, and set a new state of the art on WMT14 translation at a fraction of the training cost of previous models.
title: Attention Is All You Need
whoShouldRead: You know seq2seq with RNNs and basic softmax/linear algebra, and want the exact mechanics of the Transformer.
